components.notes: The sheet displays the {neg,to}-fragment language and Hilbert derivability by finite sequences (line 7), the three axiom schemas A1, A2, A3 (lines 8-10) and modus ponens (line 11) as registry rule displays; it is rendered on the literal reader route through \showcalculus{hilbert-cpl} (the only on-route invocation). Same named system and domain as the body definition def:p02-hilbert-derivation; no old artifact is relied on.

On the sheet itself (the registry file input by \showcalculus) a run-in heading 'Deduction theorem.' states the result in full: for every set Gamma and all formulas phi, psi of the {neg,to}-fragment, Gamma u {phi} |-_H psi iff Gamma |-_H phi -> psi, identifies it as Theorem thm:p02-hilbert-deduction ('Deduction theorem for the Hilbert calculus'), points to its written annex proof annex:p2.calc.2, and records why the premise-sensitive formula-sequence calculus satisfies it (MP is the only rule; uniform substitution only instantiates schemas). This meets the acceptance clause 'the deduction theorem stated as a named result on the sheet' and the refined remaining work 'named deduction theorem or an explicit linked statement on the sheet'.
